claims.text: Vapor-phase infiltration of a Cu precursor onto pre-formed W surfaces will produce a conformal Cu coating.
The deposited Cu coating will have atomic-scale thickness or structure.
Sintering vapor-coated W surfaces will dramatically improve Cu–W interfacial bonding relative to conventional powder infiltration or sintering.
The intervention will minimize voids relative to conventional powder infiltration or sintering.
The intervention will minimize W–Cu phase separation relative to conventional powder infiltration or sintering.
Vapor-phase infiltration can deposit a thin, uniform Cu layer on all exposed surfaces of a porous or connected W structure.
Processing below the boiling point of Cu under controlled low pressure will ensure gentle Cu deposition and subsequent sintering.
A conformal Cu coating will establish a nearly perfect, void-free Cu–W interface.
The conformal Cu coating will enhance diffusion bonding during sintering.
Reducing Cu–W interfacial defects will improve thermal transport and mechanical strength.
Vapor-deposited Cu bonds strongly to tungsten.
Atomic-scale diffusion during post-deposition sintering promotes uniform Cu–W interfacial contact.
Uniform interfacial contact produces a continuous Cu–W metal–metal bond.
A continuous Cu–W metal–metal bond prevents phase separation and void formation under reactor conditions.
The vapor-phase-infiltrated composite will have significantly higher thermal conductivity than composites made by the stated conventional baselines.
The vapor-phase-infiltrated composite will have improved mechanical durability under irradiation relative to the stated conventional baselines.
Mechanically alloyed composites and vapor-coated powders sintered without the proposed infiltration step suffer from interfacial voids and phase separation.
The intervention is applicable to high-temperature, irradiative fusion-reactor joint service.

contradictions.description: The method is described as a single-step intervention, but it explicitly requires vapor deposition followed by a separate final consolidation or sintering step.

Vapor-coated powders are treated as a deficient baseline made without vapor-phase infiltration, even though vapor coating is itself closely equivalent to the proposed vapor-phase deposition intervention; no operational distinction between the two routes is defined.

The predicted-outcome field names 'mechanical alloying of vapor-coated powders' as a comparator, whereas the baseline field separately lists mechanically alloyed composites and vapor-coated powders, leaving the actual baseline inconsistent and ambiguous.
